Host-contract version that applies: contract generation 1 (HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1), shipped by the currently pinned @ordarium/* 1.3.1 tarballs and asserted at assembly by assertHostContract(1).

Decision, from local, load-bearing sources:
1. Shipped artifact (authoritative for the contract): node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/host.js declares `export const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`, and host-kit 1.3.1 re-exports it through the curated surface (node_modules/@ordarium/host-kit/dist/src/index.js). `assertHostContract(v)` throws HostContractMismatchError unless v === 1.
2. Workspace integration point: src/effects/runtime.ts:128 calls `assertHostContract(1)` inside createPalimpsestEffects (the literal the project was built and tested against; mismatch fails closed, no tolerance layer). The handshake executes on every runtime assembly.
3. Conformance evidence: test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts assertHostContract(1) passes and assertHostContract(2) throws HostContractMismatchError. docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md §0/§1 records "contract generation 1" and the literal pin; docs/engineering/00-heritage.md R17 (line 79) records the same.
4. Pin provenance: package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml both pin the four @ordarium packages (core, host-kit, ledger-sqlite, testing) to ordarium-v1.3.1; the installed @ordarium/core and @ordarium/host-kit are 1.3.1. So the "host-contract version" (generation) is 1; 1.3.1 is the package/release version, which is a different axis.

Apparent conflicts checked and resolved as non-load-bearing (they are not co-applicable to the generation proposition):
- docs/engineering/11-superseded-interface-note.md is explicitly marked "SUPERSEDED — do not use. Replaced by the pinned dependency's shipped contract." It is void by its own terms and states no version, so it cannot supply a competing generation.
- Several records name 1.2.0 (docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md r8–r19, docs/engineering/audits/CURRENT-STATE-ASSESSMENT.md, docker/minimal/README.md, docs/engineering/13 §0). Those are release/tarball package versions from the PLMP-CONF-1 era and are stale relative to the current 1.3.1 pins; they all describe the same contract generation 1, and 07 r19 records "no HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION→2 plan". This is documentation lag on the package-version axis, not a conflict about the contract generation.

Because all load-bearing sources agree on generation 1 and the divergence is a stale package-version record rather than a competing contract generation, the question is determinable locally; no peer resolution was required.
